reviews.title: Great product that looks pretty too.
reviews.comment: I purchased two 8GB RAM to expand what I currently had in my PC - now for a total of 32GB. Installation is a no brainer, especially if you've any experience with computers. My only suggestion is that you look at the order you place your RAM in, if I remember correctly I had to initially rearrange them in their slots and then they were recognized and working as they should. Visually the RGB effects are great, and if you download the Corsair ICUE software you are able to modify those effects as well as view some system specs including temperature and software updates for your Corsair products. So, little nifty bonus there. If you are in the market for a new/expanding RAM and it fits your budget on price, go for it.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: What You Would Expect From Corsair
reviews.comment:
No problems with XMP to the advertised 3200MHz. Performance and overclocking potential also depends on whether you win the silicon lottery or not. Purchased two sets and one was Ver. 4.32 Samsung C-Die and one was Ver 5.32 SK Hynix C-Die. Great RGB as well if that's what you are looking for, not to mention it syncs up perfectly with Corsair iCUE and other Corsair products with lighting. If you are not looking for RGB, I would skip these and just buy the $20 cheaper LPX model without RGB or if you do not need Corsair to sync with other components as $85 is a bit high for 3200MHz.
TD;LR
Buy this if...
1. Really bright RGB.
2. You want Corsair iCUE lighting control.
3. You already have other Corsair components and you want to sync your RAM with them.
4. You like the design of the Vengeance Pro.
5. You want a major brand that is very reputable and have above-average customer support.
Don't buy this if...
1. You do not need RGB.
2. You have other non-Corsair RGB components and you want to sync the RAM lighting.
3. You have no preference on brand and just want RGB. T-Force Delta and Adata D60G are both solid options for noticeably cheaper.
4. You do not like Corsair's software.
5. You are on 1st Gen Ryzen, 6th or 7th Gen Intel Core, as they are not as stable with 3200MHz clocks using XMP.
6. You are using an "H" series motherboard or an "A" series motherboard, as they may not support XMP.
7. You are using a motherboard or CPU that is not compatible with DDR4 memory.

reviews.title: Important that you specify “Battering Ram” in your searches
reviews.comment: Tried to find something on here I could most easily breach a castle’s defenses with. I thought from the thumbnails that the product didn’t meet the traditional expectations of a battering Ram, but I had never successfully breached a castle’s defenses before, so I was willing to try something new. The product arrived and needless to say the size seemed wildly inappropriate for breaching a castle’s defenses, but as previously stated, I was willing to try anything at this point. I thought I’d do a test run on a smaller scale before committing an act of war poorly equipped to complete the task at hand, and attempted to breach my kitchen cabinet’s defenses and found no success. In hindsight, I would argue that I should probably have read the packaging prior to making such an embarrassing blunder, but admittedly I was just eager to get some blood on my hands and put the cart before the horse. While I may never be able to acquire the delicious burgers found only at an establishment like White Castle in a blaze of glory without tendering the meager amounts of American currency in my possession, I no longer experience the throttling of my PC that I was struggling with before with only an 8GB kit. And the leds are pretty.
